title: Reduce paging noise and harden burn-rate SLO alerts after capacity-driven SLO breach
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity pressure event on 2026-03-08 we observed sustained tail-latency increases for the hosted text generation path which breached our generation_latency_99p SLO for ~42 minutes. Multiple burn-rate alerts fired and on-call received 6 pages in a 30 minute window, many of which were duplicates caused by low-threshold burn-rate rules combined with correlated upstream autoscaling noise. This ticket captures the postmortem follow-ups focused on reducing paging noise and making burn-rate alerts more signal-rich while preserving early detection for true customer-impact incidents.
comments: 2026-03-08 — Aisha Patel: Incident INC-2026-03-08-01 — capacity pressure during node eviction. Autoscaler removed 2 GPU nodes, queue latencies spiked and we saw a 3x increase in 99p latency. Immediate mitigation: pinned runtime to previous kernel, increased capacity pool by +2. Incident declared resolved at 03:14 UTC.

2026-03-09 — Carlos Mendez: Root cause: race between autoscaler policy and bursty job churn; KV cache warmed poorly after eviction. Metrics: generation_latency_99p breached 2x target; error-rate stayed low but tail latency and request queue-length rose. On-call noise: 6 pages (4 low-severity burn alerts, 2 paging duplicates).
2026-03-10 — Priya Singh (PM): Reviewed incident doc. Requesting concrete guardrails so product teams aren't paged for transient, non-impacting spikes and to ensure ops sees true degradations.
action_items: AI-1: Increase paging burn-rate threshold for generation_latency_99p from 1.5x to 2.5x over 5m for P1 pages; retain 1.5x -> slack alerts only. Owner: Carlos Mendez. Due: 2026-03-12.
AI-2: Add absolute-error floor to burn-rate paging rule: only page when > 250 affected requests in 5m AND burn-rate>2. Owner: SRE team (oncall rotation). Due: 2026-03-15.
AI-3: Implement deduplication window for repeated burn-rate alerts per deployment (suppress identical pager for 20m). Owner: Infra Alerts eng: Mei Chen. Due: 2026-03-18.
AI-4: Create separate burn-rate channels: infra-burn (ops-only) vs customer-burn (pages). Route infra-burn to Slack with low urgency. Owner: Oncall tooling: Jamal Wright. Due: 2026-03-20.

AI-5: Add a short-lived grace for autoscaler-triggered capacity churn: if autoscaler event detected within same 2m window, mark burn-rate alerts as 'auto-scaling-correlated' and suppress paging. Owner: Runtime infra team. Due: 2026-03-22.

AI-6: Run a 2-week canary of new thresholds against production traffic and produce a signal/noise report (false-pages per week, time-to-detect true incidents). Owner: Reliability Analytics (Priya Singh). Due: 2026-04-05.
AI-7: Update runbook and oncall playbook to document the new thresholds and add troubleshooting checklist for capacity vs algorithm regressions. Owner: SRE docs: Nora Blake. Due: 2026-03-19.
progress_updates: 2026-03-11 — Carlos Mendez: Implemented threshold change in staging; running load test with synthetic burst. Observed 70% reduction in pager count for similar synthetic spikes.
2026-03-12 — Mei Chen: Small patch merged (PR #312) to add dedup window; scheduled rollout to prod during a maintenance window 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.
2026-03-13 — Jamal Wright: Slack routing config created and validated in sandbox workspace; awaiting prod ACLs from platform team.
2026-03-14 — Priya Singh: Reviewed canary plan. KPIs for canary approved: page_count, mean_time_to_detect, false_positive_rate.
acceptance_criteria: Pages for generation_latency_99p reduce by >=50% for transient capacity spikes in the 2-week canary while maintaining detection of full-degradation incidents.
No increased mean_time_to_detect for verified customer-impact incidents beyond 5 minutes.
Runbook updated and oncall team trained; post-canary retrospective completed.
